# Edible Factor

> Edible Factor is a diner app in private beta in Bengaluru that tracks your calories and your food budget at the same time. Its blog covers food price news, calorie and cost comparisons, and what labels and menus promise. Every post lists its sources.

## Site

- [Edible Factor](https://ediblefactor.com/): The only app that tracks your calories and your budget at the same time. Private beta in Bengaluru.
- [Plate by Edible Factor](https://ediblefactor.com/plate): Plate brings your restaurant menu, team, diner experience and printed materials into one workspace.
- [Blog](https://ediblefactor.com/blog/): Food price news, calorie and cost comparisons, and what labels and menus promise.

## Blog

- [Nandini Milk Price Hike 2026: What ₹8 More a Litre Means](https://ediblefactor.com/blog/nandini-milk-price-hike-november-2026): Nandini toned milk went from ₹46 to ₹54 a litre on 1 November 2026. What the KMF hike means for your monthly milk bill, your curd and your coffee.
- [Bengaluru Coffee and Tea Prices: Why Your Cup Costs ₹5 More](https://ediblefactor.com/blog/bengaluru-coffee-tea-price-hike): Several Bengaluru hotels raised coffee and tea by ₹3 to ₹5 a cup on 2 November 2026, after the Nandini milk hike. What changed, where, and what has not.
- [Mangaluru Hotel Food Prices May Rise 5 to 10%: What We Know](https://ediblefactor.com/blog/mangaluru-hotel-food-price-rise): Mangaluru's hotels association estimates food may cost 5 to 10% more as onion, rice, dal and milk climb. Nothing is decided yet. Here is the kitchen maths.
- [Idli vs Dosa Calories: Which Breakfast Is Lighter?](https://ediblefactor.com/blog/idli-vs-dosa-calories): Two idlis are about 150 kcal and one plain dosa about 125 by ICMR-NIN's table. Two tablespoons of coconut chutney add 120. Here is the whole plate.
- [Coffee vs Chai: Calories and Caffeine per Cup, by ICMR-NIN](https://ediblefactor.com/blog/coffee-vs-chai-calories-caffeine): A cup of coffee is about 110 kcal and a cup of chai about 75 by ICMR-NIN's recipes. Coffee also carries more caffeine. Most of the gap is the milk.
- [South vs North Indian Thali Calories: Which Plate Is Lighter](https://ediblefactor.com/blog/south-indian-vs-north-indian-thali-calories): Built from one ICMR-NIN guide, a South meals plate is 670 kcal and a North roti plate 750 (our sums). The cereal makes the gap. Where you eat costs more.
- [Cheese vs Paneer: Protein, Fat and Sodium Compared per 100 g](https://ediblefactor.com/blog/cheese-vs-paneer-nutrition): Per 100 g, paneer has 18.9 g protein and 18 mg sodium. US processed cheese has 18.1 g protein and 1,671 mg sodium. Same protein, about 90 times the salt.
- [Calorie and Food Budget Tracking: Every Meal Has Two Prices](https://ediblefactor.com/blog/two-budgets-one-plate): Every meal costs calories and rupees at the same moment. Why Edible Factor counts both on one screen, what the demo shows, and what we will not claim.
- [India sugar price 2026: what 34 percent does to a menu](https://ediblefactor.com/blog/india-sugar-price-rise-restaurants-2026): India's retail sugar price hit Rs 65.05 a kg on 26 August, up 34 percent in a month. What the 2026 sugar spike actually costs an independent restaurant.
- [Ferrero Rocher Is 30% Chocolate. The Label Saved It.](https://ediblefactor.com/blog/ferrero-rocher-30-percent-chocolate-what-menus-can-learn): Ferrero Rocher is 30% milk chocolate and 28.5% hazelnuts, all printed on the box. What that label means for Indian restaurants writing their own menus.
- [Lindt two lawsuits, and what your menu promises](https://ediblefactor.com/blog/lindt-two-lawsuits-what-your-menu-promises): Two separate Lindt lawsuits got merged into one online story. Pulled apart, they show what a premium word on a menu actually costs.
- [Truffles, the camera, and what restaurants get wrong](https://ediblefactor.com/blog/camera-in-your-dining-room): A staff member at Truffles told a food creator he could not film. What the reel that followed should teach restaurants about who describes their food.
